gap: No result ChatGPT got states that Soundcore's US store sells a replacement AeroClip 2 charging case ($109.99) and replacement left/right buds ($139.99), each listed as 'Compatible with Aeroclip 2', or that it still sells the first-generation AeroClip at the same $169.99 as the AeroClip 2. A shopper therefore has to check the generation, because spec-sheet call claims (Thus AI chip, 4 mics + 2 VPUs) apply only to the 2.
standout_why: I compared against Openear Club's 'Best Open-Ear Earbuds for Work' (cited by ChatGPT) and RealBuyerExperiences (cited). Openear Club already covers the angle's strongest point for this question: the OpenComm2 UC includes a USB adapter that 'presents the headset to a locked-down work machine', and all picks support multipoint. It also already says LDAC is 'Android only' on the AeroClip. It lists the first-gen 'Soundcore AeroClip' at $129.99 and does not separate it from the AeroClip 2. RBE says nothing about dongles, certification or PC use. What's left that a rival doesn't have is AeroClip generation and parts pairing. That is new but minor, and it does not decide a pick. I couldn't open the RTINGS OpenComm2 2025 review (it returned only navigation) or the Soundcore blog (HTTP 401), so I couldn't compare against them.
decides: The finding confirms our AeroClip 2 pick rather than changing it. The page should name the generation ('AeroClip 2', $169.99 at the maker on 2026-11-08) and warn that the first-gen AeroClip costs the same at Soundcore US while lacking the Thus chip and the 4 mics + 2 VPUs claims. The more decisive compatibility point would be which OpenComm2 SKU includes the USB adapter: ChatGPT's $159.95 'OpenComm2 (2025)' card versus the $199.95 UC card. But Openear Club already covers the adapter in part, and I couldn't source the SKU split from Shokz (see unsourced).
